props.characteristic: what the procedure does to the example set
props.positive_test: acts on the training examples before they reach the learner
props.negative_test: acts on parameters, gradients or outputs
props.examples: tokenization, augmentation, curriculum

props.positive_test: converts raw input into the units or features the model consumes
props.negative_test: changes which examples are present
props.examples: BPE, WordPiece, feature scaling, discretisation, spectrogram extraction, one-hot encoding

props.positive_test: emits a transformed version of an existing example for training
props.negative_test: emits an entirely new example
props.examples: mixup, CutMix, RandAugment, SpecAugment, back-translation, adversarial perturbation

props.positive_test: decides which examples are used, with what weight, in what order
props.negative_test: changes the content of an example
props.examples: dedup, quality filtering, DoReMi, curriculum learning, active learning, class-imbalance resampling

props.positive_test: assigns a target to an example that did not have one
props.negative_test: assigns targets by a human annotator inside the run
props.examples: pseudo-labelling, Snorkel, label propagation, Dawid-Skene, HER relabelling

props.positive_test: creates training examples that did not exist before
props.negative_test: transforms examples that already exist
props.examples: Self-Instruct, domain randomisation, generative oversampling, dataset distillation

props.characteristic: what determines the distribution of collected interaction
props.positive_test: determines what interaction data the learner sees, by acting
props.negative_test: consumes a fixed dataset
props.examples: epsilon-greedy, PER, self-play
props.notes: empty for any run with a static dataset

props.positive_test: decides which action is taken for data-collection purposes
props.negative_test: decides how the collected data updates parameters
props.examples: epsilon-greedy, Boltzmann exploration, UCB, Thompson sampling, RND bonus, NoisyNets

props.positive_test: decides which past interaction is replayed and with what target
props.negative_test: decides which fresh action to take
props.examples: experience replay, PER, HER, episodic memory, rehearsal buffers

props.positive_test: decides which environment, goal or opponent the agent faces next
props.negative_test: decides the action within a fixed task
props.examples: self-play, PSRO, league training, PLR, POET, automatic domain randomisation

R.fit.name: Producing or adapting the learned object

props.characteristic: which part of the fitting loop the procedure defines
props.positive_test: participates in turning data into parameters
props.negative_test: acts before data reaches the learner, or after parameters are final
props.examples: loss functions, optimisers, LoRA

props.positive_test: sets parameter values before any update
props.negative_test: changes parameters after updates have begun
props.examples: He init, Xavier init, orthogonal init, LSUV, Fixup, muP init

props.positive_test: defines the scalar the run minimises, including added penalty terms
props.negative_test: defines how that scalar's gradient is turned into a step
props.examples: cross-entropy, InfoNCE, ELBO, PPO surrogate, weight decay, KD loss, SAM
props.notes: the most crowded slot in the dimension

props.positive_test: defines how an intractable expectation or posterior is estimated or sampled
props.negative_test: defines the scalar being estimated
props.examples: REINFORCE estimator, reparameterisation trick, straight-through estimator, Gumbel-softmax, EM E-step, MCMC, variational inference, SMC
props.notes: the slot that makes classical statistics fit

props.positive_test: modifies the gradient between the backward pass and the update
props.negative_test: modifies the loss, or the optimiser's internal state rule
props.examples: gradient clipping, gradient accumulation, PCGrad, DP-SGD noise, gradient compression at the worker

props.positive_test: maps a gradient and optimiser state to a parameter change
props.negative_test: produces the gradient, or decides which parameters are eligible
props.examples: SGD, momentum, Adam, AdamW, L-BFGS, Shampoo, Muon, CMA-ES, closed-form normal equations
props.notes: Adam never fills any other slot; the slot test passes cleanly

props.positive_test: iterates a map to its fixed point, or solves for one, with no gradient of an objective involved
props.negative_test: mapping a gradient and optimiser state to a parameter change (R.fit.update); a closed-form solve in one shot
props.examples: value iteration, policy iteration, counterfactual regret minimisation, regret matching, Sinkhorn iterations, belief propagation
props.notes: added after pinning: R.fit.update's positive test demands a gradient, so these had no slot on any axis

props.positive_test: changes a hyperparameter of the update over the course of training
props.negative_test: changes the direction of the update
props.examples: cosine annealing, SGDR, warmup, one-cycle, ReduceLROnPlateau, batch-size ramps, EMA decay schedule

props.positive_test: decides which parameters are eligible to change, or adds new ones to change instead
props.negative_test: decides how eligible parameters change
props.examples: LoRA, adapters, prefix tuning, BitFit, linear probing, layer freezing, PackNet masks

props.positive_test: decides when fitting ends or which produced checkpoint is kept
props.negative_test: decides the step size while fitting continues
props.examples: early stopping, patience, best-on-validation checkpointing, trial early-stopping in Hyperband

props.characteristic: the physical resource across which the computation is laid out
props.positive_test: determines how a single logical run is physically carried out -- across workers, devices, or one device's memory hierarchy
props.negative_test: anything that changes what is computed rather than how it is carried out; a library that merely implements such a strategy
props.examples: all-reduce SGD, ZeRO, FedAvg
props.notes: renamed from R.coord after phase 1: `coordination across workers` left single-device procedures (FlashAttention, gradient checkpointing) with no slot on any axis; renamed from R.exec after pinning: `R.exec` and the attribute family `A.exec` are two senses of the word and began co-occurring in pins, the same collision as L.kernel/L.operator

props.positive_test: every worker holds the full model and processes a different data shard
props.negative_test: workers hold different parts of the model
props.examples: synchronous SGD, ring all-reduce, Hogwild!, local SGD, DiLoCo, gossip SGD

props.positive_test: the model's parameters, optimiser state or layers are split across devices
props.negative_test: the model is replicated
props.examples: ZeRO-1/2/3, FSDP, Megatron tensor parallel, GPipe, 1F1B, expert parallelism, ring attention

props.positive_test: changes what or how often workers transmit, not what they compute locally
props.negative_test: changes which worker computes what
props.examples: gradient quantization, PowerSGD, top-k sparsification, infrequent averaging, hierarchical all-reduce

props.positive_test: trades recomputation or data movement against stored state on one device
props.negative_test: trades work across devices
props.examples: gradient checkpointing, activation offload, CPU/NVMe offload, mixed precision with loss scaling

props.positive_test: combines updates from parties that do not share raw data, under a stated constraint
props.negative_test: combines gradients from workers that share one dataset
props.examples: FedAvg aggregation, SCAFFOLD control variates, secure aggregation, trimmed-mean robust aggregation

props.characteristic: which part of the configuration is searched
props.positive_test: runs or simulates multiple configurations and selects among them by a measured signal
props.negative_test: fixes the configuration in advance
props.examples: random search, Hyperband, DARTS
props.notes: the inner trials are themselves runs

props.positive_test: searches scalar or categorical settings of a fixed learning procedure
props.negative_test: searches the model's structure
props.examples: grid search, random search, TPE, SMAC, Hyperband, ASHA, PBT, muTransfer

props.positive_test: searches the structure of the model itself
props.negative_test: searches the optimiser's settings
props.examples: NASNet, ENAS, DARTS, Once-for-All, regularised evolution, zero-cost proxies

props.positive_test: searches jointly over preprocessing, model family and their hyperparameters
props.negative_test: searches within one fixed model family
props.examples: Auto-WEKA, auto-sklearn, TPOT, AutoGluon

props.positive_test: searches over which data or training procedure to apply, rather than model settings
props.negative_test: searches over the model or its scalars
props.examples: AutoAugment, Population-Based Augmentation, learned curricula, data-mixture search

props.characteristic: what is changed about the stored parameters
props.positive_test: transforms an existing parameter set without redefining what the model computes
props.negative_test: fits parameters from data in the first place
props.examples: magnitude pruning, GPTQ, model soups

props.positive_test: removes parameters or structures from the computation
props.negative_test: changes the numeric representation of retained parameters
props.examples: magnitude pruning, lottery ticket, movement pruning, SparseGPT, Wanda, channel and head pruning

props.positive_test: lowers the numeric precision of weights, activations or caches
props.negative_test: removes parameters
props.examples: GPTQ, AWQ, SmoothQuant, LLM.int8, QAT, LSQ, BinaryConnect, KV-cache quantization
props.notes: QAT also occupies R.fit.est via the straight-through estimator

props.positive_test: replaces a weight tensor with a product of smaller factors
props.negative_test: zeroes or requantises the original tensor
props.examples: SVD compression, Tucker and CP decomposition, ASVD

props.positive_test: produces one parameter set by combining several
props.negative_test: produces one by combining several models' predictions
props.examples: model soups, task arithmetic, TIES, DARE, Fisher merging, SWA, EMA of weights

R.out.name: Producing outputs from the learned object

props.characteristic: what the procedure contributes between a trained model and an emitted result
props.positive_test: runs at inference and changes what is emitted, how it is scored, or what it was given
props.negative_test: changes the parameters
props.examples: beam search, RAG, conformal prediction

props.positive_test: converts model scores into the emitted output
props.negative_test: explores multiple complete candidate outputs
props.examples: greedy, beam search, top-p, contrastive decoding, constrained decoding, speculative decoding, diffusion samplers, classifier-free guidance

props.positive_test: spends extra inference compute exploring several reasoning or action paths
props.negative_test: emits one pass through the model
props.examples: self-consistency, best-of-n, tree of thoughts, ReAct, Reflexion, MCTS, MPC/CEM, A-star
props.notes: the cost shows up in the run's budget

props.positive_test: selects external content to place in the model's input at inference
props.negative_test: selects training examples before fitting
props.examples: BM25, DPR, HNSW index lookup, RAG, FiD, reranking, kNN-LM

props.positive_test: converts outputs into calibrated probabilities, intervals or an abstention decision
props.negative_test: converts them into a different emitted answer
props.examples: temperature scaling, isotonic regression, conformal prediction, deep ensembles, MC dropout, OOD scoring

props.positive_test: combines outputs of several models or several samples into one
props.negative_test: combines their parameters
props.examples: voting, prediction averaging, stacking, MBR, Bayesian model averaging, MoE inference routing

props.positive_test: computes the output by an explicit named procedure over stored data or fitted structure, with no model forward pass to delegate to
props.negative_test: emitting the forward pass of a separable model
props.examples: k-NN majority vote, kernel density prediction, LOESS local fit, Viterbi decoding of a CRF, GP posterior mean
props.notes: added after the k-NN worked example found no fitting slot

props.positive_test: produces a statement about the model's behaviour as the run's output
props.negative_test: produces a prediction about the data
props.examples: Grad-CAM, integrated gradients, LIME, SHAP, activation patching, sparse autoencoder features, CKA
props.notes: admitted because an explanation is an output

props.positive_test: computes a reported performance or inference claim about the fitted object
props.negative_test: contributes to producing the object or its outputs
props.examples: k-fold cross-validation, bootstrap CIs, permutation tests, FDR control, LLM-as-judge scoring, significance tests
props.notes: the participant rule as written excludes this; see Tensions

props.positive_test: reorganises how a single operator is computed on one device -- tiling, fusion, recomputation, memory-hierarchy placement
props.negative_test: a different operator (linear attention changes the function and is model-side); a package that ships such a kernel
props.examples: FlashAttention, FlashAttention-2, PagedAttention, fused optimiser kernels
props.notes: the boundary case both phase-1 runs named and neither could place
